chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever seeks the pleasure of the people through the wrath of God, God will make those who praise him blame him.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who seeks people's pleasure by incurring God's wrath?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* within the chapter on character traits, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual consequence of *riya* (showing off) and the pursuit of human validation over divine pleasure. It serves as a practical warning that prioritizing societal approval at the expense of God’s command results in a divine reversal of reputation, where public praise turns to blame, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner sincerity (*ikhlas*) as the core of worship.
